- When sentiment is negative and forecast is rising, reduce forecast peak values to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is positive and forecast is falling, avoid premature downward corrections — allow slight lagged rebound.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive declines), model should not over-forecast upward correction.  
- Overshoot after sharp spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high) should be capped or smoothed with sentiment-weighted decay.  
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment is consistently negative over last 5–7 days, reduce forecast mean by 2–5% to reflect bearish bias.  
- If sentiment swings sharply upward after a dip, model should not overreact — avoid “rebound overcorrection” in early forecast days.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, forecast should not deviate more than ±3% from recent 7-day average unless strong signal.  
- Lagged corrections (e.g., forecast 30d but true outcome 10d later) should be adjusted downward if sentiment is negative — avoid “anticipation bias”.
